title: Glutathione Quantification in Live Cells with Real-Time Imaging and Flow Cytometry
author: Jiang, Chen, et al.
materials: •To prepare the staining solution, typically, the stock solution is diluted with its corresponding solvent (DMSO for RT-AM and HaloRT ligands, DI water for MitoRT) 50 times to 100 μM.•Staining solution can be stored at −20°C for 1 week. Make small aliquots if necessary.

•GSH standard solution can be prepared by dissolving GSH powder in PBS or DI water. Typical concentration of GSH standard solution is between 0.5–50 mM in final solution. Adjust pH to 7.4 by adding NaOH solution when directly dissolve GSH powder in DI water. GSH solution should be made fresh each time to minimize errors from undesired oxidation.•H2O2 working solution can be prepared by diluting from the original 30% solution using PBS to the desired concentration. The working solution needs to be made fresh each time.CRITICAL: GSH and H2O2 are both unstable due to its redox active chemical properties. Make fresh solution each time and limit their exposure to air will reduce potential errors during quantification. GSH and H2O2 solutions are primarily used for calibration thus will determine the overall performance of this protocol.•BSO stock solution (100 mM) can be prepared by dissolving BSO powder in PBS or DI water (preferred). BSO working solution can be prepared by diluting with the appropriate solvent or buffer.•NMM stock solution (100 mM) can be prepared by dissolving NMM powder in anhydrous DMSO. NMM working solution can be prepared by diluting with DMSO.•DEM stock solution (100 mM) can be prepared by diluting liquid DEM in anhydrous DMSO. DEM working solution can be prepared by diluting with DMSO.•BSO, NMM and DEM stock solution can be stored at −20°C for 3 months. Make small aliquots if necessary.

steps.title: Prepare cell cultures
steps.instruction: Obtain the required cell lines (HeLa, HT‑1080, COS‑7, HepG2, 3T3‑L1, PANC‑1, MOLM‑14, primary hepatocytes from BALB/c mice, hESC‑derived neurons) from ATCC or other sources. For imaging, grow cells on glass‑bottom dishes; for flow cytometry, keep them as single‑cell suspensions. Adherent cells: culture in a T‑75 flask with DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; seed 2.0 × 10⁶ cells per flask, allow 2–4 days to reach confluence, passage regularly, and use cells <2 months old and <15 passages. Use cysteine‑free medium when decreasing intracellular GSH with BSO or other low‑GSH conditions. Non‑adherent cells (e.g., MOLM‑14): culture in a T‑75 flask with RPMI‑1640 + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen‑strep under the same incubator conditions; seed 2.0 × 10⁶ cells per flask, reach confluence in 4–7 days, passage regularly, and use cells <2 months old and <15 passages. Primary hepatocytes: isolate from mouse liver and keep in DMEM until use (follow referenced protocol). hESC‑derived neurons: maintain in neurobasal medium (follow referenced protocol).

steps.title: Prepare staining and reagent solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare all solutions fresh and keep them on ice or at the indicated storage temperature. Staining solution: dilute the stock ligand (RT‑AM or HaloRT in DMSO, MitoRT in DI water) 50‑fold to a final concentration of 100 µM; aliquot and store at –20 °C for up to 1 week. GSH standard: dissolve GSH powder in PBS or DI water to obtain 0.5–50 mM; if dissolved in DI water, adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH; make fresh each use. H₂O₂ working solution: dilute 30 % stock with PBS to the desired concentration; prepare fresh each use. BSO stock (100 mM): dissolve BSO powder in PBS or DI water (preferred); store at –20 °C for 3 months, aliquot. Prepare BSO working solution by diluting the stock with the appropriate buffer. NMM stock (100 mM): dissolve NMM powder in anhydrous DMSO; store at –20 °C for 3 months, aliquot; dilute with DMSO for working solution. DEM stock (100 mM): dilute liquid DEM in anhydrous DMSO; store at –20 °C for 3 months, aliquot; dilute with DMSO for working solution. All redox‑active reagents (GSH, H₂O₂) are unstable; limit air exposure and prepare immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare slides and imaging dishes
steps.instruction: Coat plain glass slides with poly‑D‑lysine, then dry at 18–25 °C. The coated slides can be used for bead‑based calibration, non‑adherent cell imaging, or for culturing adherent cells similarly to glass‑bottom dishes. No additional preparation is needed for commercial glass‑bottom dishes or chamber slides. Immediately before imaging, clean the bottom of the imaging container with appropriate tools to ensure optimal image quality.

steps.title: Transfect cells for HaloRT probes (if applicable)
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours before staining, seed cells at the required density: 2.0 × 10⁶ cells per glass‑bottom dish for imaging or 1.0 × 10⁵ cells per well of a 12‑well plate for flow cytometry. Transfect with the desired HaloTag plasmid using Lipofectamine 3000 (or equivalent). For nuclear GSH measurement, use Halo‑NLS plasmid and add 500 ng DNA per glass‑bottom dish or per well. Incubate transfected cells for 24–48 hours before proceeding. A stable cell line expressing the HaloTag protein may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Stain cells with RT‑based probes
steps.instruction: Replace the existing culture medium with the appropriate working staining solution containing RT‑AM, MitoRT, or HaloRT ligand. For adherent cells, aspirate the medium and add the staining solution directly. For non‑adherent cells, centrifuge the suspension, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in the staining solution. For flow‑cytometry experiments, first generate a single‑cell suspension: detach adherent cells with trypsin, resuspend in fresh culture medium, then follow the non‑adherent staining protocol (centrifugation and resuspension). Incubate the cells in the staining solution under the following conditions: RT‑AM – 8–10 min at 18–25 °C; MitoRT or HaloRT ligand – 15–30 min at 37 °C (or 30–60 min at room temperature if a heating device is unavailable). Temperature influences probe loading homogeneity; lower temperatures reduce aggregation for RT‑based probes, while higher temperatures aid clearance of non‑specific probe for organelle‑targeted HaloRT. For non‑adherent cells (including bead‑based calibration), pipette 10 µL of the stained suspension onto a coated glass slide, cover with a cover glass, and proceed to imaging within 15 min (seal with an O‑ring if longer incubation is needed). Washing steps are generally avoided for RT‑AM and MitoRT stained cells during confocal imaging because washing can cause up to 20 % GSH fluctuation; confocal imaging can distinguish intracellular signal from excess fluorophore. For HaloRT‑ligand stained cells, wash once with fresh culture medium, incubate at 37 °C for 15–30 min, and repeat a second wash if the signal‑to‑noise ratio (S/N) is still below 5. For confocal imaging, the wash may be omitted if S/N > 5. For flow cytometry, washing can be skipped; if S/N < 5, a brief wash may improve signal.

substeps.instruction: Replace medium with staining solution (adherent vs non‑adherent handling).
Generate single‑cell suspension for flow cytometry (trypsinization, centrifugation, resuspension).
Incubate at the temperature and time specific to the probe.
Prepare imaging sample (10 µL on coated slide, cover, avoid drying >15 min).
Optional washing for HaloRT‑ligand stained cells (one or two washes, 15–30 min incubation each).

steps.title: Perform flow cytometry staining and acquisition
steps.instruction: Dispense 500 µL of the stained cell suspension into a 5 mL polystyrene tube (single‑cell suspension). Add 5 µL of the appropriate staining solution directly to the tube, vortex briefly, and incubate for the probe‑specific time (RT‑AM 8–10 min; MitoRT or HaloRT 15–30 min). Keep the incubation time identical for all samples to minimize variation. Immediately analyze the sample on the flow cytometer. Adjust the gain settings so that both the blue and green channels achieve a signal‑to‑noise ratio greater than 3 for positive and negative controls compared with the non‑stained control. Acquire data from at least 10 000 cells per sample; aim for 30 000 or more cells for optimal statistics. For quantitative work, follow the calibration section to generate a standard curve; for qualitative assessment, the standard curve may be omitted.

substeps.instruction: Place 500 µL cell suspension in a 5 mL tube.
Add 5 µL staining solution, vortex, incubate (probe‑specific time).
Run the sample immediately on the flow cytometer.
Set detector gains to obtain S/N > 3 in both channels.
Collect ≥10 000 events (preferably ≥30 000).

steps.title: Process flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Open the acquired .fcs files in FlowJo. Gate the population by forward‑scatter (FSC) and side‑scatter (SSC) to isolate single cells. Export the fluorescence intensity values for the blue and green channels of the gated single‑cell population to a .csv file. For each cell, calculate the ratio of blue‑channel intensity divided by green‑channel intensity. Identify and remove outliers that lie more than 4 standard deviations from the mean ratio. Compare the cleaned ratio values to the calibration standard curve to determine absolute intracellular GSH concentrations (or semi‑quantitative values). Automated scripts for these steps are available on GitHub (https://github.com/jinwanglab/RT-FACS-Analysis).

substeps.instruction: Gate single‑cell population (FSC/SSC) in FlowJo.
Export blue and green channel data to .csv.
Compute blue/green ratio per cell.
Remove ratios >4 SD from the mean.
Map ratios to GSH concentrations using the standard curve.

steps.title: Calibrate probe against lysate‑based GSH assay
steps.instruction: Prepare two identical sets of cells and treat them with a series of BSO concentrations (e.g., 0–500 µM for HeLa) for 48–72 hours. Culture one set in 12‑well or 6‑well plates for lysate‑based GSH measurement; culture the other set in the appropriate imaging or flow‑cytometry containers for probe staining. For the lysate set, determine GSH content using either the Ellman’s assay or a liquid‑chromatography‑mass‑spectrometry (LC‑MS) method. For the probe set, stain and image or run flow cytometry as described above, then record the fluorescence ratio for each BSO condition. Plot the ratio versus the independently measured GSH concentration and fit an appropriate function (linear or non‑linear as dictated by the data). Note that the ratio‑to‑GSH relationship may be non‑linear depending on experimental conditions; consult the cited literature for guidance on fitting models.

substeps.instruction: Treat parallel cell groups with graded BSO concentrations (0–500 µM) for 48–72 h.
Measure GSH in one group by Ellman’s assay or LC‑MS.
Stain the second group with the RT‑based probe and record fluorescence ratios.
Plot ratio versus measured GSH and fit the best function.
Use the fitted curve for subsequent quantification of unknown samples.
